introduction: God’s purpose in revealing Himself, the first reading says, “is to lay bare those gems that lie hidden within the mine of their true and inmost selves”. The readings go on to education and daily growth, to the change of fishermen into apostles, to perfection “according to kind” as the meaning of happiness, and to the promise that no lost jewel is beyond finding. Job’s miners, the treasure hid in a field, the lost piece of silver, the talents, “it doth not yet appear what we shall be” and Paul’s “perfect man” are the biblical forms. Aristotle and Mencius both made the fulfilment of a nature the measure of a life, Mencius going so far as to say “all things are already complete in us”. Gray’s Elegy mourns the gems that circumstance left in the dark, and Hamlet can recite what man is and feel nothing.
questions: The gems are “hidden within the mine”. What kinds of education do the readings think bring them out? Compare Mencius’s “all things are already complete in us”.
Gray’s villagers never had the chance to become what they might have been. What do the readings imply is owed to such people, and by whom?
Reading 19 defines happiness as “perfection according to kind or station”. How does that differ from happiness as getting what one wants?
The disciples “were unlearned and ignorant men”. What does the guide think changed them, and can that be studied or only undergone?
Hamlet knows “what a piece of work is a man” and is unmoved. What stands between knowing one’s potential and acting on it?

outside.why: Gems hidden in the mine of the true self. Job’s hymn to mining: surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold where they fine it.
The kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field.
“I have perfected in every one of you My creation.” I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
The Prophets come to nurture the trees of human existence with living water. He shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season.
Every person will advance until he manifests his potential forces. Till we all come unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ.

The purpose of God has been to bring forth the mystic gems from the mine of man. Gray in a country churchyard thinks of those never brought forth: full many a gem of purest ray serene the dark unfathom’d caves of ocean bear. He blames poverty and want of schooling. What do the readings say about the gems that stay buried, and whose task they are?
The Manifestations come to dispel the darkness of the animal nature. Be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.
To raise man to knowledge of his potentiality. Thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour.

Hamlet knows the potential by heart, how noble in reason, how infinite in faculty, and it does nothing for him: and yet, to me, what is this quintessence of dust? What must be added to knowledge of human greatness for it to move a person?
Children of the Kingdom, and the art of music. Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
Spiritual perfections must be acquired along with outward attainments. Neglect not the gift that is in thee.
“Day by day you must grow.” To act, that each to-morrow find us farther than to-day.

Whoever strives harder for the human perfections is nearer the threshold. Mencius on the mark of them: above the power of riches to dissipate, of poverty to make swerve, and of force to make bend: these characteristics constitute the great man.
Change deserts into rose gardens. The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose.
The coward becomes courageous, the debased holy. If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away.
Out of rough fishermen He made apostles. The council perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, and marvelled; and took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.
The call that began it, to men mending nets by the lake: follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
Children of God, endowed with infinite progress. Now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be.
Why the spirit appears in the body: to pass through the degrees. Rumi: I died as a plant and rose again an animal. I died as an animal and arose a man. Why then should I fear to become less by dying?

Perfection according to kind, and this perfection is happiness. Aristotle’s formula: that which is proper to each thing is by nature best and most pleasant for it; for man, the life according to reason.
A seed reaches its goal once it springs up and bears. Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit.
They have become the image of what God planned them to be. So God created man in his own image.
Souls differ in capacity; there are as many ways to God as breaths. There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit.
The ultimate result of human life, the prize. I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling.

We must rescue ourselves from the arc of descent by acting on the teachings of God. Mencius trusted what is already there: all things are already complete in us. Reading 28 says men always need one to guide them. Is the teacher’s work to add something, or to uncover it?
People at all times need someone to exhort and teach them. How can I, except some man should guide me?
What is needed in the next world must be obtained here. The master gave talents to each according to his several ability, and returned to reckon with them.
He is able to rescue wayward souls from remoteness. When he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and ran.
He bore ordeals that selflessness might appear in the world. Mencius: when Heaven is about to confer a great office on any man, it first exercises his mind with suffering.

If one speck of a jewel be lost beneath a mountain of stones, the Hand will find it. A woman with ten pieces of silver, if she lose one, lights a candle, and sweeps the house, and seeks diligently till she find it.
He which hath begun a good work in you will perform it.

shortfall: Readings 12, 18, 22, 24 and 26 are brief exhortations or exclamations on the same point as their neighbours and were left with those neighbours’ companions.
